text: The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315, its worst day in about 18 months, and the S&P 500 dropped 4.36% as selling in AI and chip stocks spread.
QQQ closed down about 6.5% at $647.05 and TQQQ fell about 19% to $50.47.
The VIX fear gauge jumped about 70% to 28.18, its biggest one-day rise since April 2025.
Treasury yields fell as investors moved into bonds: the 10-year to about 4.84% and the 2-year about 11 basis points to roughly 4.47%.
Gold rose about 1.5% to around $4,119 while silver slipped to $51.65, pushing the gold/silver ratio up to about 79.8. GDX gained 1.4% and SLV dipped 0.5%.
Brent crude rebounded $3.67 to $98.29 after tanker fires near the Strait of Hormuz.
Bitcoin fell about 6% to near $75,700 as the tech sell-off spread to crypto.
After the close, gold slipped to about $4,054 early Friday, falling alongside stocks rather than acting as a safe haven.
